name: Kota Kinabalu Marriott Hotel
short_description: Waterfront Marriott Hotels property in central Kota Kinabalu with South China Sea-view rooms, an 8th-floor infinity pool and the rooftop Stylo bar.
ai_summary: Opened in 2018, the 332-room Kota Kinabalu Marriott Hotel is a modern waterfront tower in the Sabah state capital, set beside the South China Sea and within walking distance of the Imago and Centre Point malls. Independent reviewers consistently single out the views: sea-facing rooms with balconies, an 8th-floor infinity pool overlooking fishing boats and islands, and a top-floor M Club lounge and Stylo rooftop bar that catch sunset panoramas. Rooms are contemporary and generously sized (guest rooms around 40 sqm, Ocean Suites up to 91 sqm), and elite recognition draws praise, with several Titanium members reporting suite upgrades and a well-regarded club lounge offering breakfast and happy-hour spreads. Dining spans Big Fish (seafood), Teppan Table (Japanese), Kitchen@8 (local) and rooftop Stylo. Watch-outs recur across reviews: breakfast variety is good but some found items not fresh, pool-deck and tile cleanliness drew complaints, in-room coffee/beverage provision is thin, and one points blogger felt the property trails the nearby Hyatt Regency on service and overall value at its price point. TripAdvisor rates it 4.0 of 5 (roughly 316 reviews), ranked around #24 of 131 hotels in Sabah, reflecting a strong but not flawless reputation. Best suited to travellers who prize sea views, pool time and central access over a resort-beach setting.

faqs.question: How far is the Kota Kinabalu Marriott from the airport?
faqs.answer: Kota Kinabalu International Airport (BKI) sits about 7 km from the hotel, roughly a 10 to 15 minute drive depending on traffic. The property is in the central waterfront district, so most city-centre attractions, malls and the seafront are within a short taxi ride or walk.

faqs.question: Does the hotel have sea-view rooms and a pool?
faqs.answer: Yes. Many rooms and suites face the South China Sea with balconies, and higher categories such as the Ocean Suite offer wide sea views. There is an 8th-floor outdoor infinity pool overlooking the water, plus a children's pool and a fitness centre.

faqs.question: Is the Marriott a good choice for Bonvoy elite members?
faqs.answer: Reviewers report strong elite recognition, including suite upgrades for Titanium members and access to a well-regarded top-floor M Club lounge serving breakfast and evening food and drinks. Elite members can typically take breakfast in the lounge or the pool-side restaurant.

reviews.title: Review: Kota Kinabalu Marriott (Ocean Suite)
reviews.author: Fai
reviews.summary: Points-focused stay in a 91 sqm Ocean Suite: praises modern rooms, sea views, gym and elite upgrade, but flags furniture stains, pool-side noise, weak in-room coffee and value trailing the nearby Hyatt.

reviews.title: [M'SIA HOTEL REVIEW] Kota Kinabalu Marriott Hotel 2D1N Stay Review
reviews.author: Hazel
reviews.summary: Loves the spacious 40 sqm sea-view guest room, comfortable bed and infinity pool, and rates rooftop Stylo well. Notes limited TV channels, some outside noise and distance from the town centre.

reviews.title: Hotel Marriott Kota Kinabalu: A Review of Your Stay
reviews.summary: Central king room booked at RM388 via the Bonvoy app; praises the Level 8 infinity pool, sea views and location, but criticises grubby pool tiles and slow-to-arrive hot water.
